propositions: The undeclared-paths refusal instructs users to declare paths and retry, but declaring paths changes file_impact hash and triggers a stale-material refusal on retry.

The file_impact parameter defines the scope of the attestation and is used as direct input to the plan review at four sites, so widening it retroactively broadens what a signed attestation claims to cover.
The materiality check hashes the entire file_impact list, making any mutation (additive or destructive) appear equally different with no way to distinguish harmless additions from material changes.
The remedy message must state that declaring paths is a material plan change requiring re-attestation via rebar review-plan before close can succeed.
Both the undeclared-paths and stale-material gate refusals are correct and working as designed; only the message requires clarification to prevent user confusion.
